pairs.why: A has smooth, softly glossy painted plastic like the taxi and bus, while B's rocky crater ground is full of noisy grain and its white body is flat matte.
B's bear has a fine felt-like surface with seam lines and its wood has subtle grain like the real shelf, while A's surfaces are blank and smooth; B's glossy blue target counts against it.
A's rubber is smooth with soft gloss and clean gradients like the real fins, while B adds molded ribs and faint scratches the real cards don't have.
A's satin blue plastic and soft matte keys sit nearer the real calculator's slightly matte body, while B is glossier with shiny rim highlights and hard-edged white keys.
B has finer small details and metallic-looking platters with a smooth satin plastic body like the real DJ deck, while A's body is chunky and over-glossy.
A's glass and ice are clean, stylized and smooth like the real glass, while B drifts toward photographic noise with speckled bubbles and busy refraction.
Both drum kits have the same glossy blue shells, gold metal trim and scuffed heads, so surface gives no reason to choose.
A's leaves are slightly smaller and softer, nearer the real fine leaf clusters, while B's large pointed glossy leaves read bigger and more decorative.
